extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: A comprehensive multimodal evaluation benchmark for video understanding by multimodal large language models. It contains 900 manually collected and curated YouTube videos and 2,700 multiple-choice question-answer pairs, with three questions per video. Videos span six domains and 30 categories, range from 11 seconds to one hour, and include 744 subtitle files and 900 audio files.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.citeAs: Chaoyou Fu et al. Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075v3 [cs.CV], 30 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Dataset construction comprises video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos are manually collected and curated from YouTube using a domain hierarchy informed by popular YouTube trends. The benchmark covers Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual, subdivided into 30 categories. For each category, videos are collected at short (<2 minutes), medium (4–15 minutes), and long (30–60 minutes) durations. Corresponding subtitles, if provided, and audio are also obtained. The final dataset contains 300 videos in each duration group.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Subtitles are collected if provided. Of the 900 videos, 744 have subtitles; all 900 have audio.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos are sourced from YouTube, together with their corresponding subtitles, when provided, and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: During dataset quality control, text-only questions are submitted to Gemini 1.5 Pro to identify QA pairs answerable without video content. Such questions are excluded in this phase and returned to their original annotators for revision. For model evaluation, video frames are sampled according to model-specific configurations. Gemini 1.5 Pro uses one frame per second for short and medium videos and one frame every two seconds for long videos; other models uniformly sample a specified number of frames. In subtitle-enabled evaluation, subtitles corresponding to sampled-frame timestamps are selected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning thoroughly watch each entire video and iteratively create three questions, each with four candidate answer options and a designated correct answer. The resulting 2,700 QA pairs cover 12 task types involving perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Questions must be closely tied to video content. Each QA pair is examined by a different annotator for clear language, answerability, logically consistent options, and correctness of the designated answer. Questions answerable by Gemini 1.5 Pro from text alone are returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A different annotator reviews each QA pair for clarity, answerability, logical consistency of options, and appropriateness of the correct answer. Gemini 1.5 Pro is used in a text-only quality check to ensure that video content is necessary; its text-only accuracy is reported as below 15%. Correct-answer positions follow a near-uniform A/B/C/D distribution of 25.1%, 27.2%, 25.3%, and 22.4%. Temporal difficulty is analyzed through certificate lengths on three randomly sampled videos per class: the certificate is the minimum set of sub-clips necessary and sufficient for a human verifier to confirm the annotation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three multiple-choice QA pairs per video. Each QA pair is authored by one annotator and reviewed by a different annotator.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators have strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro is used for text-only QA quality filtering, not to author the final QA annotations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Video sourcing uses a domain hierarchy informed by popular trends on YouTube. Duration distributions differ within subsets: longer videos account for a larger portion of the short subset, medium-video durations are more uniform, and long videos have a long-tailed distribution with fewer samples at greater durations. Short videos predominantly contain perception tasks, while longer videos contain more reasoning tasks. Correct-answer positions are approximately balanced across A/B/C/D at 25.1%, 27.2%, 25.3%, and 22.4%, which the paper describes as supporting unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking video understanding by commercial and open-source multimodal large language models, including image-based models supplied with multiple video frames. The benchmark supports evaluation across video domains, durations, and perception, reasoning, and information-synthesis tasks, as well as comparisons of frames-only, frames-plus-subtitles, and frames-plus-audio inputs. Evaluation requests the correct option letter and computes accuracy by extracting model outputs with regular expressions and comparing them directly with ground-truth answers, without external model judges.
